MISSION BRIEF // VAMPIRE / L3HARRIS

//L3Harris

📍Melbourne, FL

Tech: Precision strike

Platform: Self-contained weapons system

Goal: Counter drones and remotely piloted platforms for U.S. Navy littoral defense.

Ticker: NYSE: LHX

Traction: Selected by the U.S. Navy to deliver VAMPIRE systems, per L3Harris. The company also says it is delivering VAMPIRE systems to the U.S. Army.

The U.S. Navy selected L3Harris to deliver VAMPIRE counter-unmanned systems for littoral defense. VAMPIRE is a self-contained weapons solution that combines reconnaissance with precision strike against drones and remotely piloted platforms. L3Harris also says it is engineering new capabilities and ruggedizing the system for maritime conditions. Separately, the company's Wraith Shield software can be paired with VAMPIRE and Drone Guardian for layered defense.

Source: L3Harris Technologies, 08SEP26

frames.mediaQuery: Seasats Lightfish unmanned surface vessel maritime border security

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH / SEASATS

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, across the Gulf of America.

Why: Crewed patrols are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and how much area one asset can cover at a time.

Private company → Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures.

Traction: Lightfish vessels deployed in the Gulf of America, following operations on the Rio Grande since January 2026, per Seasats.

Each Lightfish is about 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds. It runs on solar power, can stay on station for multiple months, and two people can launch it from a boat ramp or a pickup truck. Seasats says its payload bay has carried cameras that see in visible and infrared light, signals gear and sonar.

Seasats announced on Oct. 2, 2026 that a Lightfish fleet has been deployed to support U.S. maritime border security work, adding to an autonomous surveillance program run by the Pentagon's homeland defense office. The vessels launched from the Texas coast and will conduct persistent autonomous surveillance, carrying the program's work from the southern border into open water.

Assistant Secretary of War for Homeland Defense and Americas Security Affairs Mark R. Ditlevson said industry partners such as Seasats help "secure our nation's complex maritime domain."

Source: PR Newswire (Seasats), 2 Oct 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Spc. Jacob D. Harrell

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

fields.benefit_headline:
FINDS ITS WAY
HOME WITHOUT GPS

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // SKYDIO X10D

//Skydio

📍San Mateo, CA

Tech: Contested-environment drone

Platform: Small unmanned aircraft system

Goal: Keep a small drone flying and returning when GPS and communications are jammed.

Why: Operators can keep sensing and navigating in environments where satellite navigation and radio links are degraded.

Private company → Backers: Not stated in source.

Traction: Source lists Blue UAS Cleared list status and deployment time under 40 seconds, per Skydio.

Skydio's product page describes the X10D as a small unmanned aircraft system with a multiband radio that can switch channels, visual inertial odometry for navigation in GNSS-denied or spoofed environments, and Anchor Points for vision-based return navigation. It also lists NightSense navigation in darkness, IP55 dust and water ingress protection, and up to 45 mph top speed in stable air.

The page also describes fully offline operation and AES 256 encrypted links, and states the system is NDAA compliant and assembled in the U.S. These are manufacturer claims from the product page and have not been independently tested in this post.

Source: Skydio, product page (undated).

Image: U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Frederick Barnes

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

media.credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Frederick Barnes

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // COYOTE BLOCK 2C+RM

//Raytheon

📍Tucson, AZ

Tech: Counter-drone interceptor

Platform: Interceptor upgrade

Goal: Defeat current and emerging drone threats with a faster-launching Coyote interceptor.

Why: A tactical rocket motor aims to shorten engagement times and allow faster successive shots.

Ticker: NYSE: RTX

Traction: Three Raytheon-funded developmental tests completed, with first launches of a Coyote effector equipped with a tactical rocket motor, per Raytheon.

Raytheon says it took the Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrade from concept to testing in 15 months. The upgrade pairs a new seeker and warhead with a motor that speeds up launch and flight. Raytheon describes the work as support for an urgent joint U.S. military mission against drones.

These are developmental tests, not fielding. Raytheon says earlier Coyote variants have intercepted hundreds of drones in combat.

Source: RTX, October 12, 2026

Image: RTX (courtesy)
